## TL;DR

Reviewed the task create and edit controls and their existing fixture coverage. The primary gap was that the responsive WebKit dependency-picker test covered phone and desktop but omitted the requested tablet width. Added 768 px to the browser viewport matrix and recorded the QA scope and outcomes in `docs/qa/2026-11-task-create-edit-qa.md`.

## Work and rationale

I first confirmed the assigned worktree and clean branch, then read the task specification and inspected the task drawer’s creation and details templates. Manual creation includes title, optional body, type, priority, area, assignee, dependency selection and screenshot selection. The create action is disabled without a title. The details form includes editable dependency, type, priority and area controls. The screenshot picker uses the shared dropzone and pending attachment list, with retry/removal states and a keyboard-accessible formats hint.

I followed the repo’s existing headless WebKit test pattern rather than introducing a new browser harness. The responsive dependency-picker test already checked long titles did not widen the option list at narrow and desktop widths; adding the tablet width makes the test align with the task’s exact target matrix. Existing component tests exercise dependency filtering, self-exclusion, add/remove emissions, priority validation, and in-place title editing including keyboard save/cancel behavior. I documented these existing checks and the scope in the requested QA document.

## Approaches tried

I looked for an existing full end-to-end drawer browser harness and found that browser tests are generally focused on isolated UI behavior, while the drawer’s create/edit behavior is covered by Vue component tests. I kept this change within the established testing style: extend the existing WebKit responsive test and rely on directly relevant component-level interaction tests. The test remains headless and skips only when the WebKit executable is not installed, consistent with neighboring tests.

## Challenges and blockers

The task asks for complete create/edit flows and screenshot attach using fixtures. The codebase’s available tests split that coverage across focused component suites rather than one browser-driven flow. I did not claim a live upload or real-device result. The QA document states that the evidence is fixture and headless-browser based and identifies live server/device/image upload as out of scope for this run. No layout or dead-control defect was evident from the reviewed implementation or the test suite.

## Key learnings

The manual create and details edit paths share the same custom select and area picker components, while dependency selection has a dedicated overflow browser test and component interaction tests. The responsive test initially missed the tablet breakpoint even though the task explicitly names it. Keeping viewport expectations in the test itself ensures future picker changes are checked at 375, 768 and 1280 px. Screenshot selection has clear pending, retry and removal UI states; those states should not be described as proof of a successful external upload unless an actual upload outcome is observed.
